finding_key: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts::xml injection into the exported pptx: nominally-numeric element fields are interpolated into drawingml attributes unescaped while the write boundary never type-checks element `data`
evidence: Verified in the supplied sources: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:25-29 interpolates lumMod/lumOff/tint/shade/alpha raw into DrawingML attributes while the adjacent srgb arm (~line 35) uses escapeXmlAttr, and text.ts does the same with lvl/marL/indent/spcPct. The write-boundary half also holds: assertValidElement/assertValidSlide in packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts check only id/type/frame and id/layoutId/background/elements/notes, so element `data` (including a string in a nominally-numeric color mod) reaches Yorkie unvalidated, and the diff (pptx-actions.ts + slides-export-button.tsx) newly makes exportPptx reachable from the editor. I rate impact low because the attacker must already have deck write access, and [Content_Types].xml plus all .rels parts are generated by PptxWriter independently, so the worst realistic outcome is a corrupt or content-injected archive, not relationship/macro injection; I could not inspect model/migrate.ts, but the CLI export path bypasses it regardless.
